left.raw_text: 1. Clinical diagnosis of post herpetic neuralgia, with pain persisting for at least 3 months after the onset of herpes zoster rash
2. Clinical diagnosis of distal painful polyneuropathy due to Type I or Type II diabetes mellitus with:
1. symmetrical, bilateral pain in the lower extremities for at least 3 months
2. diabetes under control for at least 3 months prior to randomisation, as indicated by a glycated haemoglobin level (HbA1c) of ≤ 11% (97 mmol/mol)
and on a stable dose of insulin or oral diabetic medication for 3 months prior to screening

right.raw_text: and 3. no change in diabetic medication planned for the duration of the study

left.raw_text: 3. Positive sensory symptoms (mechanical or thermal) associated with neuropathic pain, confirmed by:

right.raw_text: and 2. Clinical assessment, showing signs of neuropathic pain in either a dermatomal (PHN) or distal symmetrical distribution (DPN)

raw_text: 8. An average daily pain score on the NPRS of at least 4 and no more than 8 in the last five diary entries before randomisation
